identity.system_type: set of early experimental mobile ad hoc networks
identity.core_characteristic: packet-switched wireless networking between mobile nodes without requiring a central station
historical_significance: Early experimental mobile ad hoc networking system
Demonstrated packet-switched store-and-forward radio communications in a mobile environment
Developed technologies for multi-hop communication among mobile vehicles
Participated in the first major three-way internetworking demonstration connecting packet radio, packet satellite, and terrestrial packet networks

relationship_to_internet_history.role: experimental component of the early Internet internetworking research environment

research_and_design_objectives.primary_goal: Investigate the feasibility of using packet-switched, store-and-forward radio communications to provide reliable computer communications in a mobile environment.
research_and_design_objectives.design_challenge: PRNET addressed a significantly harder networking problem than earlier systems such as ALOHAnet because it required multi-hop communications between mobile vehicles without a central station.

inspiration.significance: The earlier ALOHAnet served as an inspiration for PRNET.

distinguishing_problem.PRNET_problem: Multi-hop communication between mobile vehicles without a central station.

bob_kahn_initial_conception.architectural_concept: The overall system design was predicated upon an array of low-cost repeaters.
bob_kahn_initial_conception.repeater_definition: A particular kind of packet radio equipped to retransmit by radio some or all packets that it receives by radio.
bob_kahn_initial_conception.terminology_caveat: The source uses the historical term 'repeater', but the described function corresponds more closely to a router or packet switch than to a conventional simple radio repeater.

role: hosted first PRNET in San Francisco Bay Area

nodes.primary_mobile_nodes: Mobile vehicles and associated packet-radio terminals

routing_model.purpose: Allow packets to traverse multiple radio nodes in a mobile network.
routing_model.routing_control: Radio network routing control software was present by 1977.

gateway_capability.description: By 1977 the PRNET software included a gateway to other networks.

network_measurement.description: By 1977 the software included network measurement functionality.

debugging.description: By 1977 the software included debugging tools.

configuration.description: By 1977 the software included configuration tools.

radio_hardware.network_role: Provided the radio communications hardware used to build the early PRNET experimental networks.

quasi_operational_network.prerequisite: Prototype networking software had been developed shortly beforehand.

internetworking.importance: PRNET became part of the experimental environment in which distinct packet networks were interconnected.

three_way_demonstration.demonstration_description: A mobile vehicle in PRNET was linked with nodes in the ARPANET and, through SATNET, with nodes in London operated by Peter Kirstein's research group at University College London.
three_way_demonstration.historical_significance: The demonstration represented an early practical demonstration of internetworking across heterogeneous packet networks and was the first three-way demonstration linking ARPANET, PRNET, and SATNET.

post_demonstration_operation.relationship_to_arpanet: PRNET was usually attached to the ARPANET afterward.
post_demonstration_operation.purpose: This allowed BBN software developers in Cambridge to access and update the PRNET.

mobile_packet_radio_model.core_problem: Reliable computer communication among mobile vehicles using radio links.

historical_importance.modern_conceptual_relationship: The source characterizes PRNET as an early experimental mobile ad hoc networking system.

citation_quality.description: The supplied Wikipedia article explicitly carries a maintenance notice stating that it needs more citations.

scope: This record preserves the supplied article's content rather than independently validating every historical claim.
The source gives selected deployment counts rather than a complete inventory of PRNET nodes.
The source describes PRNET as experimental mobile ad hoc networking rather than a single fixed network with one immutable architecture.
The source does not provide a complete protocol specification.
The source does not provide a complete hardware inventory for every PRNET generation.

terminology.repeater: Bob Kahn's historical use of 'repeater' describes a radio device that can retransmit received packets; the article notes that in modern terminology this might be regarded as a router or packet switch.

fort_bragg.source_characterization: The September 1979 deployment information is explicitly attributed to Ron Kunzelman's report as quoted in IEN 121.

historical_relationships.internet: PRNET was one component of early internetworking experiments; it should not be treated as synonymous with the Internet itself.

record_integrity.historical_status: PRNET is treated as a historical experimental networking project rather than a currently operating network.
record_integrity.important_distinction: PRNET refers to a family/set of evolving experimental packet-radio networks and technologies rather than a single permanently fixed network configuration.
